newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister opposes youth curfews.
newsitem.headline: French minister opposes youth curfews.

text.p: A leading French cabinet minister said on Monday that youth curfews ordered by some towns with petty crime problems would not cure juvenile delinquency but would plunge troubled families into more difficulty.

"I don't believe in these show-off measures. They don't solve anything and all they do is point a new accusing finger at people who already have problems," Employment and Solidarity Minister Martine Aubry told France-2 television.

Conservative municipalities in Dreux and Gien, west of Paris, Sorgues in southern France, and Aulnay in the Paris suburbs have all ordered midnight curfews in the past few days for youths under 13 or under 12 years old.

They aim to prevent a repeat of previous "long hot summers" where youths in crowded high-rise suburbs and mostly of North African immigrant origin have clashed with police or vandalised property during the school holidays.
Several of the towns ordered that under-age youths be taken to a police station for their parents to come and get them, while others instructed police to take the children straight home.

The main representatives of the Paris central government in the areas where the curfews were imposed have challenged the orders in court on the grounds that they restrict civil liberties and that final legal decisions are pending. A court at Dreux has banned the imposition of the curfew for the time being.
Junior Schools Minister Segolene Royal, a Socialist like Aubry, indignantly said at the weekend that the curfews were like measures to curb stray dogs.
